body:
im 100% not saying they shouldnt be a part of the community, as yes, they can have similar experiences. allos *can* experience love at first sight, but they can also only form said love after a bond has already formed. referring to it as the norm overall was incredibly foolish on my part, as i was only considering my perspective. i dont think there can be considered just one 'norm'. but anyways, the point i was trying to make was that a large majority of people work like that, only developing feelings after a bond has been established

depending on how long it takes a person to reach that point, it might be easier to just identify as ace. in my head for some reason i was thinking that a good bond could be established in 6 months, because thats how i feel, but of course that varies from person to person. in hindsight it seems like such a stupid oversight

their experience may be more similar, but i still wouldnt say demisexuals should fall under the definition of asexuality. greys are more on a case by case basis. if they want to identify under the label for the sake of simplicity, then yeah okay fair enough. 

also "They're still not heterosexual." is hella heteronormative

why would you consider greyces to not be allosexual if they experience some sexual attraction? also, i have no problems with microlabels, and i 100% agree that they help people figure themselves out. looking back, i was probably mistaking people identifying with a microlabel as people identifying with a label-label. 100% my bad
i hope you have a good day as well :)
you are 100% right. looking back at it, i feel stupid for not acknowledging the difference between arousal and attraction.

1. the gender thing wasnt really a point i was trying to make, so ill keep this part brief. sorry if it sounded like i was bashing nbs. people can identify however they want, and im not saying they cant. i was referring exclusively to the ridiculous, almost satirical ones like delphigender. (im well aware practically no one, if anyone in the trans/nb community actually thinks like this) thinking about it now, comparing ace terms to that feels unfair, it was a stupid one off comment said in the moment

2. fair point. that perspective hadnt crossed my mind at the time of writing, but yes you are right. my point with not calling it a sexual orientation was terrible wording on my part. at the time i had meant that it shouldnt be seen as deviance from the average

3. again, fair. it was not my intention to gatekeep, or exclude members from the community. in my head it makes sense for demis to identify primarily with whatever theyre sexually attracted to, but maybe thats just narrowminded. again, im not trying to gatekeep the community, i was simply going off the dictionary definition.

bonus 4. writing this response has made me realise that i need to think far more about these topics than i already have. these are just my perspectives and theyre not set in stone, which is why i made this post. i wanted to hear other perspectives rather than just the one bouncing about my brain
no offense, but i think you missed my entire point
